holding_summary: Plaintiff was a monthly tenant of a room in a tenement house owned by the defendant company, which regularly let rooms in its buildings by the month. When she moved to a different room with the permission of the person managing the property and was later injured on a porch, the court held she was not a trespasser and that a tenant of a room, absent agreement to the contrary, has the use of the porches accessible from it in common with the other occupants.

quotes.text: The defendant owns a number of tenement houses in which it lets rooms by the month.
renting a room in the house, she had the use of the porches accessible therefrom, in common with the other occupants of the premises, in the absence of agreement to the contrary

A lessee of a room, who took possession of a room other than the one rented, by permission of one in charge of the property as a sort of superintendent, factotum, and go-between, was not a mere trespasser, as far as liability for personal injuries was concerned.

holding_summary: Von Behren privately owned a lakeside 'camp,' a platform and house that he leased for recreation to all comers, including for single days, and separately arranged for a caretaker to occupy and rent it out when not otherwise let. When a visitor was injured by the collapse of the connecting wharf, the court held the owner liable in tort for failing to keep the wharf safe, regardless of whether the injured person was a direct lessee or a guest.

holding_summary: Plaintiff, injured when defective steps collapsed, was found to be not a sub-tenant but a roomer or lodger of the defendants' tenant, who occupied a rear room under a monthly rental. Because the tenant's written lease shifted to her the duty of keeping the premises safe (absolving the owners except for neglect after notice), and because a lessee cannot convey to those claiming through her a greater right than she herself possesses, the owners were held not liable to the lodger.

quotes.text: the plaintiff was not a sub-tenant, but simply a roomer or lodger of the tenant of the property at the time of the accident
under a monthly rental she was occupying a rear room on the premises

A lessor, may, by contract, shift from himself to his lessee the duty imposed upon him by the .general law of seeing to the safety of the building owned by him, and may thus absolve himself of all duty toward others on the premises, through license or invitation granted them by the lessee.
A lesee cannot convey to others on the premises leased by him a greater right than he himself possesses.
